title: Juan Manzo Will Ask the FGR to Take Over the Case of Carlos Manzo’s Murder
author: José Shaddai Olvera Torres
content:
_This article by[José Shaddai Olvera
Torres](https://elchamuco.com.mx/author/shaddai/) originally appeared in the
[August 26, 2026 edition of El
Chamuco](https://elchamuco.com.mx/2026/08/26/juan-manzo-pedira-a-fgr-atraer-
caso-del-asesinato-de-carlos-manzo/), a Mexican satirical and political
magazine._

The brother of the murdered former mayor of Uruapan accused Samuel “N” of
surveilling him and noted that the detainees’ defense would be financed with
public funds.

Juan Manzo, brother of the murdered former mayor Carlos Manzo, backed the
accusations made against people linked to the case and charged that Samuel “N”
also monitored the former mayor’s movements to later report them to Grecia
Quiroz.

Manzo also denounced that the defense of the bodyguards detained for the
murder would be financed with public funds from the Uruapan City Council.

The accusations were raised by the former mayor’s brother amid the questions
about the investigation into the homicide.

## They Will Ask the FGR to Take Over the Investigation

Faced with what he described as inconsistencies and alleged obstacles in the
local investigation, Juan Manzo announced that he will formally request that
the Attorney General’s Office (FGR) take over the case.

The request would seek to transfer the investigation to the federal level to
review the circumstances related to the homicide of Carlos Manzo and the
accusations that have arisen around people linked to his administration.

In an interview with Milenio, Juan Manzo also maintained that the defense of
those detained for the murder would be paid by Grecia Quiroz and the
Movimiento del Sombrero.

The former mayor’s brother argued that the FGR’s intervention would make it
possible to review the inconsistencies that, according to his version, exist
in the local investigation.

### Accusations Pending Clarification

Juan Manzo’s statements correspond to accusations that will have to be
corroborated by the authorities.

The material provided does not include documents, judicial rulings, or
statements from the people named that would confirm the accusations about the
surveillance of Carlos Manzo or the alleged use of public funds to finance the
detainees’ defense.
